messages:
ops-bot: Incident detected — GPU allocation failures in GCP region us-west1. Autoscaler failing to provision GPU nodes; queue growing. Severity: P1. Paging on-call. :rotating_light:

oncall-bot: Pager fired to @cameron, @sara. Runbook: /runbooks/gpu-scaleup. Steps: confirm error, attempt fallback, escalate to cloud support. :alarm_clock:

cameron: I'm on it. seeing a spike in queue length for inference-ingress. Requests hitting 429/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. Quick snapshot from the autoscaler logs:

```

2026-03-15T22:10:03Z autoscaler controller ERROR scaleUp failed: googleapi: Error 403: Quota 'GPUS' exceeded for project 012345678901 on region us-west1, quotaExceeded

2026-03-15T22:10:15Z autoscaler controller WARN backoff timer active, next attempt in 30s

```

cameron: Confirmed customers seeing elevated latency and intermittent 503/429s. Queue length +420 requests, avg wait > 30s.

sara: Adding context — we pushed a burst of reserved warm-pool requests for a large customer at 21:55 UTC; their workload used a new high-memory GPU flavor. That probably pushed us into a hard quota wall rather than opportunistic throttles.

lee: I can attempt temporary routing to eu-west1 if capacity there is OK. But cross-region latency for some customers will be worse. I can prepare a quick policy flip in the router: set region preference fallback to eu-west1 for eligible routes.

priya: If we can't get quota in time, mitigation plan: 1) degrade large model to smaller quantized variant for best-effort customers, 2) enable response streaming to reduce tokens generated, 3) apply per-tenant soft-limits to limit queue growth. I can push the model-swap for the big tenant now if we agree.

dylan: We should also check fairshare settings — looks like the scheduler's weight for the bursty tenant is high. Lowering their weight will free slots for others. Command: `curl -XPOST https://infra-api/internal/fairshare/adjust -d '{"tenant":"big-corp","weight":0.2}'`

cameron: Running quick checks. GCP quotas: `gcloud compute regions describe us-west1 --project=redwood-prod --format=json | jq '.quotas[] | select(.metric=="GPUS")'` shows usage 100% and pending increase state is false.

cameron: Opening support case with GCP: https://console.cloud.google.com/support/cases/CASE-987654321. Case created, severity set to 'S0 - Critical' and contacted via chat. ETA unknown. Attached request: temporary quota bump or quota propagation fix.

ops-bot: Quick mitigation checklist from runbook applied: 1) scaling back warm-pool increase — done, 2) disable non-critical background batch jobs — done, 3) apply per-tenant soft-limit — in progress.

lee: Router policy change ready. Will flip pref to eu-west1 for the following routes: `/v1/generate` for non-enterprise tenants. Applying now: `http PATCH https://router.internal/policy prefer_region=eu-west1 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"`

priya: Pushing model swap for big-corp to quantized variant v2-q128. Command I'm running now:`rc deploy --tenant big-corp --model v2-q128`

cameron: Observability: token-per-request dropped ~30% for swapped tenants. Queue reduced from 420 -> 210 within 6m. Latency improved slightly but still > SLO for some.

dylan: Lowered fairshare for big-corp to 0.25. That freed a bunch of queued requests and prioritized burst distribution.

sara: Customer support notified and SOC message prepared. CC: account team. Draft status update to customers: "Experiencing degraded performance in us-west1 due to GPU provisioning limits; mitigation in place and we're routing traffic where possible. Next update in 30 minutes."

cameron: Still seeing autoscaler attempts fail with a different GCP error now: `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Operation not permitted — rateLimitExceeded`. Looks like we hit per-project request rate caps during concurrent provisioning. Log excerpt:

```

2026-03-15T22:18:47Z compute API ERROR quota API: requests per minute exceeded for region us-west1: rateLimitExceeded

2026-03-15T22:19:12Z autoscaler controller INFO retrying createInstanceGroup (backoff)

```

lee: Ok — two simultaneous issues: (1) GPUS quota reached, and (2) provisioning rate-limits preventing further attempts. For immediate relief: routing + model-swap + fairshare lowered buys us time. Longer term we need GCP support and quota increases.

priya: Also started a fallback to run smaller shards on CPU for low-priority workloads — reduces GPU pressure. Doing a rolling config to queue classifier: `config set inference.cpu-fallback=true --scope=low-prio`

ops-bot: Status update event: posted to #statuspage: "Investigating GPU provisioning failures impacting inference in us-west1 — mitigations active."

cameron: GCP support confirmed case escalated, an engineer joined — they say quota looks normal on their end but provisioning rate-limits are being throttled due to recent API spike. Support recommended staging provisioning attempts and avoiding concurrent instance-group creates. They offered a short-term exemption window of ~15 minutes to let queued requests drain.

sara: Great. Let's schedule a controlled provisioning ramp: staggered create calls with 20s spacing and reduced parallelism. cameron can you implement a quick backoff change in the autoscaler config?

cameron: Yes patching autoscaler backoff to: `maxConcurrentCreates=2, createInterval=20s` and restarting controller now.

```

kubectl -n infra exec deploy/autoscaler -- curl -XPOST http://localhost:8080/config -d '{"maxConcurrentCreates":2,"createInterval":"20s"}'

```

cameron: Patch applied. Monitoring provisioning attempts.

dylan: We're seeing sustained decrease in creation-rate errors. Queue now ~80, latency trending down. Will continue to monitor for the exemption window to close.

ops-bot: Customer impact summary (automated): ~6% of queries returned errors/timeout over last 30m, 18% experienced >2x SLO latency. Affected tenants: mix of best-effort and some mid-tier customers. No enterprise SLA breaches detected yet.

sara: Update for account teams — send targeted messages to mid-tier customers impacted and advise degraded-mode fallback option. Log customer contacts in the incident doc.

cameron: GCP engineer confirmed exemption window extended by 10m. We should avoid mass reattempts when it ends. Will keep autoscaler conservative.

lee: I've left the router fallback active but limited to non-enterprise tenants. If GCP recovers we'll revert.

priya: Final step I'm running: re-enable some batch jobs at low concurrency to avoid starvation of online requests.

cameron: Queue is under 20 and stable. Autoscaler created 6 nodes successfully during the ramp window. We'll hold here. Will keep GCP case open and request permanent quota increase for the specific GPU type. Case: CASE-987654321.

sara: I'll take the handoff to the night crew. Handoff notes: what we did, GCP case link, router fallback active, autoscaler backoff config, fairshare lowered for big-corp, model swap for big-corp to v2-q128.

sara: Handoff to @sara (night oncall). If anything regresses, page the oncall group and escalate to cloud-support. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Handoff acknowledged. Handoff metadata: incident_id=INC-20260315-392, severity=P1, handoff_time=2026-03-15T22:22:10Z, owner=sara.

ops-bot: Closing the immediate page. We'll continue monitoring and follow up with a post-incident writeup tomorrow including timeline, root cause analysis, and remediation: request permanent quota increases, autoscaler throttling strategy, warm-pool sizing guardrails. :memo:
